output.title: Spot duplicate emails before they become cleanup work
output.body:
If duplicate emails are showing up, the real question is not “can AI fix this?” It is whether duplicates reach you before you act on them. That is the bounded workflow decision: do you need early detection, or is this just cleanup after the fact? If duplicates arrive before action, the cost is usually review time, inconsistent replies, or later manual reconciliation. That is enough reason to look at the process, and not enough reason to automate blindly.

Start with three recent examples. For each one, note where it came from: a system syncing the same contact twice, the same person sending again, or you copying a thread into another tool. Then mark which duplicates must be caught before action and which can wait. An invoice or payment request belongs in the first group; a newsletter usually does not. Human approval stays in place for anything involving money or other high-risk decisions.

One practical next step is a one-week manual test. Route suspicious duplicates to a single folder and review them by hand. Count only the repeats, the false positives, and the time your own review takes. If the pattern is messy, that is useful too; it means the next step is a clearer definition of “duplicate,” not a bigger tool. Small problem, small test, no drama.
